newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh approves eight merchant banks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh approves eight merchant banks.

text.p: Bangladesh has granted eight financial institutions permission to act as merchant banks, in a move to boost a capital market dogged by allegations of share price manipulation, government officials said on Sunday.
They said a cabinet committee on finance and economic affairs, headed by Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria, on Saturday approved in principle the setting up of the banks.

The eight institutions are ANZ Grindlays Bank, American Express Bank, the government-owned Sonali Bank, General Insurance Company, and the privately owned Prime Bank, Dhaka Bank, leasing company IDLC and Progati Insurance Company.
The move follows protests last week by hundreds of traders in the unofficial kerb market against falling stock prices.
No firm date has been set, but SEC officials said formal approval was expected some time in April.
Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, the governor of the central Bangladesh Bank, said the move was intended to shore up investor confidence.
"Now, there will be institutional support in the market," he told Reuters on Saturday night. He added the banks could act as underwriters to issues and launch their own mutual funds.

The market has been jolted by a government-sponsored enquiry which found 20 market players were involved in price manipulation on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) between July and November last year. The DSE benchmark index rose to more than 3,600 points during the period and has since fallen below 1,100. On Saturday it closed up 81.02 points at 1,238.6.

Haroonur Rashid, chairman of the DSE's Securities and Exchange Commission told Reuters in a recent interview the regulatory body had ordered stock dealers to give up their directorship of listed companies with a view to preventing the possibility of manipulation.
"It is necessary to remove conflicts of interest, to ensure better transperency and stop the possibility of manipulation," he said.
